Independent primary checks. (1) Ordered configuration torsor: for a smooth curve family, the relative ordered distinct n-point configuration stack maps to the relative reduced-support effective-divisor / unordered configuration locus by forgetting order; over reduced support this is a principal S_n-bundle (finite étale S_n-torsor). For n=6 this is exactly the content of corroborated FND-0064 and the packet bottleneck line requiring an ordered finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open. (2) Stack-only / coarse failure: S_n acts on the ordered marked/configuration stack by permuting labels. On the stack this yields a torsor/quotient presentation of the unordered model. On coarse moduli, curves whose automorphisms permute the support of a reduced divisor create residual stabilizers, so the map between coarse spaces is not a free degree-|S_n| étale torsor at those points (standard free-vs-nonfree finite group action dichotomy; cf. also M_{g,n} vs M_{g,[n]}=M_{g,n}/S_n). (3) Rational descent: for any finite group G and any Q[G]-module V, the Reynolds averaging projector (1/|G|)∑_g g gives a canonical isomorphism V^G ≅ V_G; for a finite étale G-cover (or proper G-action) one has H^*(unordered;Q)≅H^*(ordered;Q)^G≅H^*(ordered;Q)_G. Thus ordered→unordered cohomology/weight descent is harmless over Q once invariants (or coinvariants) are taken. (4) Integral and coarse failures: over Z, |G| is not invertible so invariants need not equal coinvariants and the transfer multiplies by |G|; Edidin arXiv:1006.2364v2 Thm 4.40 proves H^*(DM quotient stack;Q)≅H^*(coarse;Q) and A^*⊗Q comparisons, while Example 4.46 shows the integral comparison fails (e.g. A^*(M_{1,1})≅Z[t]/(24t^2) vs A^*(P^1)≅Z[h]/(h^2)). Hence integral-coefficient or naive coarse-space rewrites of a C66-TATE-* argument built on the Conf_6 model require independent justification, while the campaign’s Q-target remains open provided stack/orbifold cohomology and S_6-invariants are used.
